chunks: And it was narrated from Yāsir al-Khādim that he said:

Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام passed by me while I was praying on the ṭabarī, and I had placed something on it. So he said to me, “What is the matter with you that you do not perform sajdah on it? Is it not from the vegetation of the earth?”

key_terms.الطَّبَرِيِّ: a type of mat or woven material referred to in the narration
key_terms.الْخَادِمِ: the servant or attendant; part of the narrator’s designation

ai.seo_question: Can sajdah be performed on something made from the vegetation of the earth?
ai.summary: This hadith indicates the permissibility of performing sajdah on something that is from the vegetation of the earth. It appears in the context of prayer rulings and clarifies what may be used for prostration.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.831 - It was narrated from the Yāsir al-Khadim that He said:

"Abu al-Hasan (as) passed by me while I was praying on a piece of ṭabarī (a mat) upon which I had placed something.
Imam (as) said to me: 'Why do you not prostrate on it? Is it not from what the earth produces?'"
